extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and IP practitioners working with Brazilian patents (INPI) and litigation
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements for filing, prosecuting, maintaining, challenging, and litigating patents in Brazil before the INPI and courts, including substantive patentability criteria, formal filing rules, timelines, and administrative/judicial review paths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent grant conditions and issuance of letters patent
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent is granted after the application is approved and the payment of the corresponding fee is proven, with the issuance of the respective letters patent (Article 38 of the LPI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment of the fee and evidence must be made within 60 days of the granting date (Article 38(1)). A patent is deemed granted on the date of publication of the respective act (Article 38(3)). The letters patent must contain the number, title and nature of the patent; the name of the inventor; the holder’s identification and address; the term of validity; the specifications; the claims; the drawings; and the data relating to priority (Article 39).

rubrics_metrics.name: Territoriality of patent rights
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent is valid only in the countries in which it has been applied for and granted protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each country is sovereign to grant a patent or not, regardless of the decision in other countries on corresponding patent applications (Article 4bis of the Paris Convention).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory contents of a patent application (formal filing requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application must contain: I – request; II – specifications; III – claims; IV – drawings, if applicable; V – abstract; and VI – proof of payment of the filing fee (Article 19 of the LPI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articles 22–26 and INPI Normative Rulings No. 30 and 31 regulate filing conditions. Forms are available on the INPI website. Minimum conditions for accepting an application include technical content, application, and proof of payment; if insufficient but containing key data, the applicant may be given 30 days to meet requirements (Article 21).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficient disclosure / written-description requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The object of the patent must be sufficiently described in the specifications, clearly and completely, to allow its reproduction by a person skilled in the art and must indicate, when appropriate, the best way to execute it (Article 24 of the LPI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When biological material is essential and not publicly available, the report must be supplemented with a deposit at an authorized institution (or an international deposit authority recognized by the Budapest Treaty) before the filing date; such data must integrate the specifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: State of the art and novelty requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: For novelty to exist, the object must be beyond the state of the art, which refers to everything made accessible to the public before the filing date (Article 11(1) of the LPI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State of the art includes written or oral description, use or any other means, in Brazil or abroad, with exceptions in Articles 12, 16 and 17 and excluding industrial secrets. The full content of a not-yet-published application filed in Brazil is considered state of the art from filing or priority date for novelty analysis (Article 11(2)–(3)). The INPI recommends a preliminary search before filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grace period for certain disclosures by third parties
rubrics_metrics.description: If a third party discloses the invention in the 12 months preceding the filing/priority date based on information obtained from the inventor (or disclosed by the INPI based on such information), a grace period is considered and the disclosure will not affect novelty (Article 12).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The INPI may require a statement from the inventor concerning the disclosure, possibly accompanied by evidence, under regulation conditions (Article 12(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority date rules and evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The priority date is the date of filing. Priority claims may be supplemented within 60 days by other priorities prior to the filing date (Article 16).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority claims must be supported by appropriate documents (number, date, title, specifications, and, if applicable, claims and drawings) with translations as required. If proof is not presented at filing, it must be provided within 180 days (or 60 days in some national-processing cases). Failure to provide evidence within time limits results in loss of priority (Article 16(7)). For international (PCT) filings, translations may be due when national processing starts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to exploit patent / compulsory licensing for nonuse
rubrics_metrics.description: Within three years of the grant of the patent, the patent holder must start exploiting or commercializing the product and exercising their right, otherwise the holder may be subject to having the patent compulsorily licensed (Article 68(5) of the LPI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A compulsory license may lapse for lack of exploitation if, after two years from the first compulsory license, nonuse is not justified (Article 80).

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential processing of national-defense-related applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent applications whose subject matter is of interest to national defense are processed confidentially and are not subject to the standard provisions of the LPI (Article 75).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless expressly authorized, it is prohibited to file or disclose abroad such an application; exploitation and assignment depend on prior authorization of the competent body. Indemnity is guaranteed when rights are restricted (Article 75(2)–(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication timing and content of publication
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application is kept secret for 18 months from the filing date or earliest priority date, after which it is published, except as provided in Article 75 (Article 30).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication may be brought forward at applicant’s request; publication must contain identifying data and make available specifications, claims, abstract and drawings. In specified cases, biological material becomes available upon publication (Article 30(1)–(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration of applications and patents (reinstatement)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent holder may request restoration of an application or patent within three months from the date of publication of the shelving in the RPI or from the expiry of the patent, proving payment of the annual fee and restoration fee (Article 87).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to request restoration leads to definitive shelving.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-issuance corrections and administrative nullity
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no specific law for correction of a granted patent; administratively, it is possible to request administrative nullity before the INPI as governed by Articles 50–55 of the LPI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nullity may be declared administratively when legal requirements are unmet or other statutory grounds apply; procedures are detailed in Articles 50–55.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative proceedings time limits and counting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Time limits for administrative proceedings are continuous and automatically extinguish the right to act after expiry, unless a just cause is proven (Article 221). Start day excluded and due date included (Article 222). Time limits start from the first business day after notification (Article 223). If no express determination, 60 days is the default term (Article 224).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judicial acts related to patents are governed by the CPC which has its own counting rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals in administrative phase (deadlines and effects)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals against INPI decisions may be filed within 60 days (Article 212). Appeals are entertained with supersedeas and full review effects and are decided by the INPI’s president (Article 215).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A decision that determines final dismissal or that grants the application/certificate of addition is not appealable (Article 212(2)). Petition/appeal will not be entertained if late or not accompanied by proof of payment of the fee (Articles 218–219). Interested parties are notified to submit briefs within 60 days; INPI may impose requirements to be met within 60 days (Articles 213–214).

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation / power of attorney requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any attorney regularly enrolled with the Brazilian Bar Association may act in the administrative stage before the INPI. Foreign applicants must appoint and maintain an attorney-in-fact in Brazil with powers to represent them in administrative and judicial proceedings (Articles 216–217).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Power of attorney must be in Portuguese (original, transcript or authenticated photocopy). Consular authentication/notarization is not required. POA must be submitted within 60 days from the date of the first act in proceedings under penalty of dismissal; dismissal of the patent application is final (Article 216(1)–(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial formal examination and remedy window
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt, minimum conditions for accepting the application are verified (technical content, the application and proof of payment). If insufficient but with necessary data, the applicant may be given a dated receipt establishing requirements to be met within 30 days (Article 21).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal requirements publication uses Order Codes (e.g., 2.5 for formal requirements needing correction); failure to meet requirements within 30 days leads to filing not accepted and numbering canceled (Article 20).

rubrics_metrics.name: Request and timing for substantive examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The substantive examination must be requested by the applicant or by any interested party within 36 months of the filing date, under penalty of the application being dismissed (Article 33).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon notification of dismissal (Order Code 11.1), applicant has 60 days to pay a reinstatement fee together with a request for examination to restore the application (Article 33(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and conduct of substantive examination
rubrics_metrics.description: During technical examination a search report and opinion are prepared concerning: I – patentability of the application; II – suitability of the application given the nature claimed; III – reformulation of the application or division; and IV – technical requirements (Article 35).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Searches are conducted by engineers and technicians specialized in patent system and technological fields; they check wording against legal standards and the state of the art worldwide. Any interested party can submit comments and documents during this stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination results, requirements and response periods
rubrics_metrics.description: If the exam opinion ascertains non-patentability or lack of suitability, or makes any requirement, the applicant will be notified to provide comments within 90 days (Article 36). If requirements are not met, the application is definitively dismissed (Article 36(1)). If answered (even if not entirely satisfied) or contested, the examination proceeds (Article 36(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Possible exam conclusions: patentable (Order Code 9.1); adaptation/reformulation/division/technical requirements (Order Code 6.1); unpatentable (Order Code 7.1). Requirements must be met within the period determined by Article 36 (90 days).

rubrics_metrics.name: Documents and evidence to be submitted during examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Once examination is requested, within 60 days, whenever requested, the applicant must submit: I – objections, search for prior art and examination results for corresponding applications abroad when priority is claimed; II – documents required for regularization and examination; and III – simple translation of priority documents replaced by a declaration, when applicable (Article 34).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to provide requested items within 60 days can lead to dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments before examination allowed but limited
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may amend the application up until the request for examination, provided that the amendments are limited to the subject matter initially disclosed in the application (Article 32).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments after request for examination are constrained by Article 32 limitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration and effects of patent nullity (grounds and consequences)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent nullity is declared administratively when: I – any legal requirement has not been met; II – specifications and claims do not comply with Articles 24 and 25; III – the subject matter extends beyond the content of the application originally filed; or IV – any essential formalities to granting were not met during processing (Article 50).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partial nullity is possible if remaining claims are patentable by themselves (Article 47). Nullity takes effect from the filing date (ex tunc) (Article 48). An action for nullity may be filed by the INPI or any person with legitimate interest within six months from grant; nullity proceedings continue even if patent term has expired (Articles 51 and 51(1)). Due process applies, holder has 60 days to respond; INPI president issues decision and publishes it when final and unappealable (Articles 50–57).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and monitoring via RPI and PUSH-INPI
rubrics_metrics.description: INPI acts, orders and decisions are published in the RPI; a table of codes and numerical index allow identification of application progress. Users must monitor their applications through the RPI with the assigned application number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants can register processes in PUSH-INPI to receive publications by email (but PUSH-INPI does not replace RPI monitoring). Specific Order Codes indicate stages (e.g., Order Code 2.10 for request notification; 3.1 for publication after 18 months; 9.1 for granting notification; 11.4 for extraordinary payment period to evidence grant fee payment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal and abandonment publication and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: A withdrawn or abandoned patent application must be published (Article 29). A request for withdrawal must be submitted within 16 months of the filing date or earliest priority date (Article 29(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawal of a previous filing without producing any effect gives priority to the immediately subsequent filing (Article 29(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural grounds that will render petitions/appeals inadmissible
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition will not be entertained if submitted after the time limit or not accompanied by proof of payment of the respective fee (Article 218). Petitions/opposition/appeal will not be entertained when late, lacking legal grounds, or not accompanied by proof of payment (Article 219).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The INPI will, when possible, take advantage of parties’ acts and establish appropriate requirements (Article 220).
